factValues.name: gr:ParaIndex_2675_fv
factValues.value:
The principal activity of the Company is that of the provision of administrative support to other group companies.

								Company name change

								On 19 November 2024 the Company passed a resolution to change its name from Tellurian LNG UK Ltd to Woodside Energy (LA) UK Ltd.

								Results and dividends

								The Company recognised a net loss after taxation of $1,903,017 for the year ended 31 December 2024 (2023: net loss after taxation of $2,549,466). No amounts have been paid or declared as dividends during the course of the financial year and the directors do not recommend the payment of a dividend in respect of the financial year.

factValues.name: gr:ParaIndex_2979_fv
factValues.value: In our opinion, Woodside Energy (LA) UK Ltd (formerly Tellurian LNG UK Ltd)’s financial statements:

factValues.name: gr:ParaIndex_26665_fv
factValues.value: The financial statements have been prepared under the historical cost convention unless otherwise specified within these accounting policies and in accordance with Financial Reporting Standard 101 'Reduced Disclosure Framework'  and the Companies Act 2006.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35416_SectionEnd_35462_SectionUID_1417444292_ParaIndex_35437_fv
factValues.value:
Turnover is measured as the fair value of the consideration received or receivable, excluding discounts, rebates, value added tax and other sales taxes.
								
							Rendering of services
								
							Turnover is recognised on a cost plus 15% basis, in line with the intercompany service agreement with a fellow group company. Intercompany turnover is recognised when all of the following conditions are satisfied:
								
							the amount of turnover can be measured reliably;it is probable that the Company will receive the consideration due under the intercompany service agreement;the costs incurred under the intercompany service agreement can be measured reliably.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35539_SectionEnd_35542_SectionUID_1417444795_ParaIndex_35539_fv
factValues.value: The Company's functional and presentational currency is USD.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35545_SectionEnd_35556_SectionUID_1417444838_ParaIndex_35545_fv
factValues.value:
Foreign currency transactions are translated into the functional currency using the spot exchange rates at the dates of the transactions.
								
							At each period end foreign currency monetary items are translated using the closing rate. Non-monetary items measured at historical cost are translated using the exchange rate at the date of the transaction and non-monetary items measured at fair value are measured using the exchange rate when fair value was determined.
								
							Foreign exchange gains and losses resulting from the settlement of transactions and from the translation at period-end exchange rates of monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are recognised in profit or loss.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35576_SectionEnd_35581_SectionUID_1417442206_ParaIndex_35578_fv
factValues.value: Finance costs are charged to profit or loss over the term of the debt using the effective interest method so that the amount charged is at a constant rate on the carrying amount. Issue costs are initially recognised as a reduction in the proceeds of the associated capital instrument.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35671_SectionEnd_35676_SectionUID_1416238752_ParaIndex_35671_fv
factValues.value:
Defined contribution pension plan
								
							The Company operates a defined contribution plan for its employees. A defined contribution plan is a pension plan under which the Company pays fixed contributions into a separate entity. Once the contributions have been paid the Company has no further payment obligations.
								
							The contributions are recognised as an expense in profit or loss when they fall due. Amounts not paid are shown in accruals as a liability in the Balance Sheet. The assets of the plan are held separately from the Company in independently administered funds.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35771_SectionEnd_35819_SectionUID_1580911917_ParaIndex_35771_fv
factValues.value:
The Company as a lessee
								
							The Company assesses whether a contract is or contains a lease, at inception of a contract. The Company recognises a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability with respect to all lease agreements in which it is the lessee, except for short-term leases (defined as leases with a lease term of 12 months or less) and leases of low value assets. For these leases, the Company recognises the lease payments as an operating expense on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease unless another systematic basis is more representative of the time pattern in which economic benefits from the leased asset are consumed.
								
							As a practical expedient, IFRS 16 permits a lessee not to separate non-lease components, and instead account for any lease and associated non-lease components as a single arrangement. The Company has not used this practical expedient.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_35853_SectionEnd_35864_SectionUID_1471444450_ParaIndex_35855_fv
factValues.value:
Tangible fixed assets under the cost model are stated at historical cost less accumulated depreciation and any accumulated impairment losses. Historical cost includes expenditure that is directly attributable to bringing the asset to the location and condition necessary for it to be capable of operating in the manner intended by management.
								
							At each reporting date the Company assesses whether there is any indication of impairment. If such indication exists, the recoverable amount of the asset is determined which is the higher of its fair value less costs to sell and its value in use. An impairment loss is recognised where the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount.

factValues.name: gr:SectionStart_36346_SectionEnd_36359_SectionUID_1555586163_ParaIndex_36346_fv
factValues.value:
The preparation of financial statements in accordance with FRS 101 requires management to make judgements, estimates and assumptions that affect the application of policies and reported amounts of assets and liabilities, income and expenses. Estimates and judgements are continually evaluated and are based on historical experience and other factors, including expectations of future events that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances.

There are no key sources of estimation uncertainty.

factValues.name: gr:ParaIndex_110961_fv
factValues.value: There were no adjusting or non-adjusting events occurring between the end of the reporting period and the date these financial statements were approved.
